1 حَذَتِ الشَّفْرَةُ النَعْلَ , [aor. and inf. n. as below,] The shoemaker's knife cut the sandal, or sole. (S.) And حَذَى يَدَهُ He cut, or cut off, his arm, or hand, (T, S, K,) with a knife. (S.) And حَذَى أُذُنَهُ He cut off a piece of his ear. (TA.) ―
-b2- حَذَى الجِلْدَ, aor. يَحْذِى, He, or it, wounded the skin. (TA.) And حَذَى الإِهَابَ, (K,) inf. n. حَذْىٌ, (TA,) He rent, or tore, much, or he made many holes in, the skin, or hide. (K, TA.) ―
-b3- حَذَى لِسَانَهُ, (S, Mgh, K,) and فَاهُ (S) or فَمَهُ, (TA,) aor. as above, (S, Mgh, Msb,) and so the inf. n., (S, TA,) (tropical:) It, namely, vinegar, and wine, or beverage, (S, Mgh,) and [sour] milk, (Mgh, K,) &c., (K,) bit his tongue, (S, Mgh, K,) and his mouth; (S, TA;) had a burning effect upon it, like cutting. (Mgh.) ―
-b4- حَذَى فُلَانًا بِلِسَانِهِ (tropical:) He spoke evil of such a one, saying of him what would grieve him if he heard it; reviled, vilified, or vituperated, him; (K, TA;) [as though] he cut him with his tongue. (TA.) A man who does so is termed ↓ مِحْذَآءٌ . (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also what next follows.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
